traits.leaf_arrangement.note: DELTA (read 2026-10-16): alternate in Polygonaceae (nearly always), Chenopodiaceae (usually), Tamaricaceae, Plumbaginaceae, Cactaceae (Pereskieae; areoles spiral); opposite in Caryophyllaceae and Nyctaginaceae (usually); Aizoaceae either. Close split; alternate first by summed species, inferred. APweb gives no order-level state.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: DELTA (read 2026-10-16): Polygonaceae, Chenopodiaceae, Tamaricaceae alternate and spiral; opposite pairs in Caryophyllaceae, Nyctaginaceae, much of Aizoaceae (overrides).

traits.leaf_division.note: APweb, Caryophyllales page, order characterisation (read 2026-10-16): lamina margins entire. DELTA: Tamaricaceae simple (scale-like); all families with candidates state simple.

traits.flower_symmetry.note: DELTA (read 2026-10-16): flowers regular in Caryophyllaceae, Amaranthaceae, Chenopodiaceae, Nyctaginaceae, Aizoaceae; Cactaceae regular or somewhat zygomorphic.

traits.ovary_position.note: DELTA (read 2026-10-16): superior in Caryophyllaceae, Amaranthaceae, Polygonaceae, Nyctaginaceae, Tamaricaceae; Cactaceae inferior; Aizoaceae superior to inferior.

traits.carpels.note: APweb, Caryophyllales page (read 2026-10-16): gynoecium of three carpels, styles long, as the order's starting state. DELTA: Caryophyllaceae 2-5, Polygonaceae (2-)3(-4), Tamaricaceae (2-)3-4(-5), Nyctaginaceae 1; Cactaceae 3-100 (states its own).

traits.fruit_type.note: APweb, Caryophyllales page (read 2026-10-16): fruit a loculicidal capsule at order level. DELTA: capsules in Caryophyllaceae, Aizoaceae, Tamaricaceae; nut or achene-like in Polygonaceae, Chenopodiaceae, Nyctaginaceae; berry in Cactaceae.

traits.sexual_system.note: DELTA (read 2026-10-16): mostly hermaphrodite in Caryophyllaceae, Amaranthaceae, Chenopodiaceae, Polygonaceae, Cactaceae, Aizoaceae; Tamaricaceae hermaphrodite or dioecious; APweb: Nepenthaceae dioecious.

traits.life_span.note: DELTA (read 2026-10-16): Cactaceae perennial; Aizoaceae, Chenopodiaceae, Caryophyllaceae annual to perennial; Tamaricaceae woody; Polygonaceae herbs, shrubs, trees. 'Usually perennial' inferred by species weight (cacti, mesembs, woody taxa).

traits.rosette.note: DELTA (read 2026-10-16): leafy-stemmed herbs and shrubs in Caryophyllaceae, Chenopodiaceae, Tamaricaceae, Nyctaginaceae; basal rosettes in parts of Plumbaginaceae, Droseraceae, Montiaceae (stated). Inferred.

traits.hypanthium.note: DELTA (read 2026-10-16): hypanthium absent in Tamaricaceae, Nyctaginaceae; present or absent in Polygonaceae, Cactaceae, Aizoaceae.

traits.flowering_position.note: DELTA (read 2026-10-16): Caryophyllaceae inflorescence terminal (dichasia); Polygonaceae, Chenopodiaceae, Nyctaginaceae terminal or axillary; cacti lateral from areoles (override). 'Usually terminal' weighted by Caryophyllaceae; medium confidence.

traits.inflorescence.note: DELTA (read 2026-10-16): Caryophyllaceae dichasial cymes; Chenopodiaceae and Aizoaceae cymose; Amaranthaceae spikes or heads.

rules.appearance.organs.basal.shape.peti.note: How PlantGen draws a rosette leaf's stalk (Caryophyllales families, 2026-10-19), the stem leaf's rule (kingdom Plantae) for the rosette's: the forb's rosette card is already sized to blade and petiole together (basal_length), but no rule gave the petiole its share, so round-leaved sundew's 0.7 cm blade was drawn 4 cm long and 5 cm wide. Stated for the order first; 18 built-in rosette species with a stated petiole would change if it moved to Plantae.

generator.defaults.nodes.why: A herb's stem bears as many leafy nodes as its year's leaves fill: one leaf to a node where they alternate, a pair where they are opposite, a whorl's count where they are whorled; a campion's or a four o'clock's stem carries eight to twelve pairs, not the herb program's five nodes.

rules.generator.defaults.nodes.note: How PlantGen counts a Caryophyllales herb's leafy nodes from the leaves its stem bears (Caryophyllales families, 2026-10-19), a choice of the model's: first renders of 12 herbs of the order drawn on the herb program's 5 nodes looked bare beside the floras' leafy stems (Silene vulgaris, Mirabilis jalapa, Phytolacca americana, FNA vol. 4-5). Stated for the order's herbs first; the rule holds for any herb and could move to the forb form.

appearance.organs.basal.shape.petiole.why: A rosette leaf's card holds the blade and its stalk end to end, as a stem leaf's does: a sundew's small round blade at the end of a stalk four times its length.
